title: Backend: expose historical indicator + signal time series for charting
description: docs/architecture/Frontend.md §5 documents this exact gap and explicitly flags it as a future backend task: `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history` returns raw OHLCV bars only, and `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` returns indicator/screen/signal values for the *latest* bar only — neither exposes a historical time series, which is why PriceChart.tsx currently plots candlesticks only with no indicator overlay (see that component's own doc comment). This task is that future backend work, now wanted: add a way for the frontend to get indicator values (at minimum ema_13, ema_26, macd_histogram, bull_power, bear_power, stochastic_k, force_index_2ema per docs/Analyse.md §4's Indicator Summary Table) AND the resulting signal (per docs/Analyse.md §5) for each historical bar, not just the latest one, so the UI can plot them over time. Decide the endpoint shape as part of this task (e.g. extend GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history with an optional indicator/signal series, or add a new GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators?range=... endpoint) — record as a decisions entry with rationale, keeping in mind this must not duplicate indicator math in a second place (compute once in the backend's existing signal engine, per Architecture.md §3's 'one place, testable once' principle already cited by Frontend.md §5).

checklist.step: Decide the endpoint/response shape for historical indicator+signal data (extend /history vs. a new endpoint; which fields; whether to include weekly-screen-derived fields like tide/impulse per bar or only the daily indicators) and record as a decisions entry.
Implement the endpoint/response change in backend/app/api/, reusing the existing signal engine (backend/app/signals/) rather than recomputing indicator math separately.
response_model, error responses (404/422/503 etc.), operation_id, summary, docstring, and Pydantic field descriptions per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard.
Hand-computed or fixture-backed reference-value tests confirming the historical series values match the existing single-point /analysis values for the same date (no drift between the two).
Run `python scripts/export_openapi.py` from backend/ and commit the updated backend/openapi.json.

Update docs/architecture/Frontend.md §5 to reflect that historical indicator/signal data is now available (it currently documents the gap this task closes), and update backend/app/api/schemas.py field descriptions accordingly.

decisions.decision: Added a new endpoint, GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators?range=..., rather than extending GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history with an optional indicator/signal series.
decisions.rationale: Keeps /history's existing job (raw OHLCV, cheap, always-available) unchanged for the common case (a plain candlestick chart with no indicator overlay) instead of making every /history caller pay for a much more expensive computation (analyse() re-run per bar) whenever indicators aren't actually wanted. A new resource also gets its own operation_id/response_model/error contract cleanly instead of a conditional shape on an existing one. Rejected alternative: an `include_indicators=true` query flag on /history that changes its response shape conditionally -- rejected because OpenAPI/TypeScript can't cleanly express a response shape that depends on a query param's value without a discriminated union the generated client would have to branch on, and because it conflates two different performance profiles under one contract.

decisions.decision: Each point includes the 7 raw indicator values (ema_13, ema_26, macd_histogram, bull_power, bear_power, stochastic_k, force_index_2ema) plus the resulting signal, confidence, and confidence_band -- but NOT the full screens breakdown (tide/impulse/wave/trigger objects) that /analysis exposes for its single latest-bar snapshot.
decisions.rationale: The description's minimum bar (docs/Analyse.md §4's table) is exactly these 7 values, and 'the resulting signal' per docs/Analyse.md §5 is the BUY/SELL/HOLD label -- confidence/confidence_band were added too since app.signals.engine.analyse() already computes them as part of the same SignalResult at zero extra cost, and they let a future chart color/size signal markers by conviction. The screens sub-objects (tide.trend, wave.state, trigger.reference, etc.) were left out of the per-bar response to keep this endpoint's primary use case (charting) lean -- IndicatorsPanel.tsx already renders the full screens breakdown for the latest bar via /analysis, and nothing in this task's description or the two frontend follow-on tasks (frontend-chart-signal-overlay, frontend-oscillator-chart) asks for a historical screens time series. Can be added later as additional optional fields without a breaking change if a future task needs it.

decisions.decision: app.signals.engine.analyse_history() passes the SAME (untruncated) weekly_ohlcv to every per-bar analyse() call, rather than truncating it to only the weeks that had 'already happened' as of each daily bar's date.
decisions.rationale: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis has never point-in-time-truncated weekly data for its own 'today' call -- it always uses whatever weekly series the provider currently returns. Truncating weekly_ohlcv per day would actually break this task's own required invariant (checklist item 4, 'the historical series' last point matches /analysis for the same date'): app.data.stooq_provider.StooqProvider._resample_weekly labels each weekly bar with its W-FRI (Friday) date, so the current, still-forming week's bar can be labeled with a not-yet-reached Friday date relative to the latest available daily bar -- a naive '<= bar_date' truncation would incorrectly drop that in-progress week even at the series' very last point, disagreeing with /analysis. Practical effect: Screen 1/Tide is held at its current value across the whole returned series (documented in analyse_history()'s docstring and in API.md/Frontend.md), while Screen 2/3, the Impulse gate, and every listed daily indicator still vary bar to bar as expected. Rejected alternative: truncating weekly_ohlcv to whole completed weeks only (dropping the in-progress week entirely rather than keeping/discarding it wholesale) -- rejected as unnecessary added complexity for a charting endpoint, and because it still wouldn't match /analysis's own (also not point-in-time-strict) latest-bar behavior, which is what checklist item 4 actually pins down.

decisions.decision: No `interval` query param -- GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators always computes daily-cadence indicators/signals, unlike /history which supports both `daily` and `weekly`.
decisions.rationale: Every indicator/Screen this endpoint returns (docs/Analyse.md §4's table entries 1-5, all marked 'Daily' or 'Weekly & Daily' but consumed here at daily resolution) plus the BUY/SELL/HOLD signal itself are evaluated at daily cadence by app.signals.engine.analyse() -- a 'weekly' variant would require a materially different computation (weekly EMA/MACD/Elder-Ray and a weekly-cadence signal definition Analyse.md doesn't define), not just a different resample of the same values. Out of scope for this task; can be added as a separate endpoint or param later if a weekly chart resolution is actually wanted.

decisions.decision: The `range` query param trims which already-computed points are RETURNED, but every returned point is still computed from the full available daily history (not from a pre-trimmed frame) -- so indicator warm-up (EMA/MACD/Stochastic needing prior bars) is always correct even for points near the start of a trimmed window. Accepted the resulting O(range_size x full_history_length) per-request cost (bounded by the default range=1y, worse for range=max on a ticker with many years of history) as a known, documented limitation rather than solving it in this task.
decisions.rationale: Pre-trimming daily_ohlcv to the requested range before looping would degrade (NaN-tail) the earliest emitted bars' indicators, which would be a worse, silent correctness bug for a charting feature whose whole point is to show real indicator values over time. The performance tradeoff is bounded by the default range (1y, ~252 bars) matching /history's own default, and yfinance/Stooq-scale histories (thousands of bars for old tickers) only get expensive under an explicit range=max request -- acceptable for MVP scope; if it becomes a real problem, a caching layer or a lower-level vectorized recomputation of just the daily-cadence pieces (not re-deriving Tide, which doesn't change per bar here) would be the follow-up, not something to build speculatively now.

decisions.decision: Fixed the Screen 1 (Tide) look-ahead bias review finding by truncating weekly_ohlcv per bar in app.signals.engine.analyse_history() to only the weekly bars as-of the CALENDAR WEEK (Saturday-through-Friday, matching StooqProvider._resample_weekly's W-FRI labeling) containing each daily bar's own date, via a new _weekly_through_bar_date() helper -- rather than either the previously-rejected naive `<= bar_date` filter or the prior (now-reverted) decision to pass the same full weekly_ohlcv to every call.
decisions.rationale: The original decision rejected per-day weekly truncation because a naive `<= bar_date` filter would drop the current, still-forming week's weekly bar (labeled with a not-yet-reached Friday per W-FRI resampling) even at the series' own most recent point, breaking the 'last point matches /analysis' invariant. Truncating by the Friday of the calendar week CONTAINING bar_date instead of by bar_date directly resolves this without special-casing: every day within the same week maps to the same cutoff (that week's Friday), and for the most recent daily bar specifically, that cutoff is -- by construction, since weekly_ohlcv was itself built via the same W-FRI resample keying -- exactly the label of weekly_ohlcv's own last row, so the filter is a no-op there and the invariant holds automatically. Verified both properties directly: (1) a synthetic weekly series with a real BULLISH-to-BEARISH flip (rising 5%/week for 20 weeks, then falling 10%/week) shows an early historical bar (within the still-bullish run) correctly reporting tide=BULLISH via analyse_history() even though the full/current series has since flipped to tide=BEARISH -- the look-ahead bug this fixes; (2) the last point in analyse_history()'s output still exactly matches a direct analyse() call's screens.tide for every existing and new test fixture, including the new flip fixture. Rejected alternative: truncating to only whole completed weeks (dropping the in-progress week outright) -- rejected again as unnecessary complexity that still wouldn't match /analysis's own last-point behavior. Also fixed the two non-blocking findings while in these files: removed the dead `hasattr(bar_date, 'date')` branch in app/api/routers/stocks.py (bar_date is always a real pd.Timestamp from a DatetimeIndex here), and removed an unrelated pre-existing unused `import pytest` in tests/unit/signals/test_engine.py (caught by ruff while editing that same file). The O(range_size x full_history_length) performance finding is left as documentation/tracking only on api-stocks-indicator-history-followups, per the reviewer's own non-blocking classification -- truncating weekly_ohlcv per bar adds a bounded, cheap additional cost (a boolean index filter over at most a few hundred weekly rows) on top of that existing, already-accepted tradeoff, not a new performance concern.

comments.summary: Round-2 re-review, confirms the round-1 blocking finding is resolved: the new `_weekly_through_bar_date()` helper truncates weekly_ohlcv per bar to the weekly bars whose W-FRI label falls on or before the Friday of the calendar week (Saturday-through-Friday) containing that bar's own date -- verified by hand for all 7 weekdays against pandas' actual `resample('W-FRI')` binning (Sat/Sun correctly map to the *upcoming* Friday, matching the resampler's own bin assignment), and confirmed the 'last point matches /analysis' invariant holds by construction (the most recent daily bar's cutoff always reduces to weekly_ohlcv's own last label). Ran the new regression tests directly: test_tide_recomputed_as_of_each_bar_date_not_held_at_todays_value (an early bar within a synthetic 20-week bullish run correctly reports BULLISH even though the full/current series has since flipped BEARISH -- the exact look-ahead bug this closes), test_last_point_still_matches_todays_full_series_tide, and test_earlier_bar_sees_fewer_weekly_bars_than_a_later_bar, all passing. Also confirmed evaluate_tide's existing NEUTRAL fallback for <2 weekly bars handles the now-possible very-short truncated windows for early historical bars gracefully (no raise). Methodology check against docs/Analyse.md §2 (Screen 1/Tide, 'never trade against the tide'): sound -- a historical point now reflects only weekly data that had actually occurred as of that bar's date, consistent with the no-look-ahead framing the rest of the endpoint already followed.

Both round-1 non-blocking findings folded into this fix as reported: the dead hasattr(bar_date, "date") branch in stocks.py is removed (now bar_date.date() directly, confirmed by reading the file), and the unused `import pytest` in test_engine.py is gone. Marked done on api-stocks-indicator-history-followups. The remaining non-blocking finding (O(range_size x full_history_length) cost of analyse_history(), worse for range=max) is unchanged by this fix and remains open on that follow-up task, correctly -- the added per-bar weekly truncation is a cheap boolean-index filter on top of the existing accepted tradeoff, not a new performance concern.
